title: Dominic and the Prom
premise: Wren Ravensworth, a nonbinary baker's kid who channels unspoken feelings into bread, has survived high school by being forgettable—until a group chat called 'The Crumb' starts posting messages about things that happen days before they occur. The chat's members—Dominic, the prom committee president hiding his own secrets; Priya, a skeptic; and Theo, Wren's ex-best friend—are bound by whatever is writing through their phones. As the predictions turn personal and dark, foretelling a fire at the spring formal, Wren must choose between protecting their invisibility and saving the people they've come to love. In the end, Wren realizes the chat was never predicting the future—it was showing them the future they'd build if they kept hiding—and by choosing to show up, speak, and be seen at prom, they rewrite it.
about_author: Astrid Iversen grew up above her family's bakery in coastal Maine, where she learned that bread can say what people cannot. She writes tender, slightly strange stories about queer kids finding their people, and still judges towns by the quality of their rye.

chapters.title: Proofing
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A quiet morning in the bakery establishes Wren's ritual of baking emotions into loaves—the grief loaf for Mrs. Okafor, the apology sourdough no one eats. At school, Wren dodges prom posters and Dominic Hale's easy smile. Emotional beat: comfortable loneliness mistaken for safety.

chapters.title: The Crumb
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren is added to a group chat of five strangers by accident—or so it seems. The first message reads: 'The blue hydrangeas die Thursday.' They do. Wren tells no one, but checks the chat eleven times that night. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into fascination.

chapters.title: Rye and Regret
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo, Wren's former best friend, reveals the fallout of their middle-school rupture from his side—he said something cruel to survive, and has regretted it since. He recognizes Wren's handwriting on a bakery order form and hesitates over the keyboard. Emotional beat: guilt with nowhere to go.

chapters.title: Second Prediction
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The skeptic of the chat, Priya tries to debunk the hydrangea prophecy and fails spectacularly when the second message—a car crash on Mill Street—comes true to the minute. She starts a spreadsheet. Emotional beat: terror disguised as methodology.

chapters.title: Flour on His Hands
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Prom committee president Dominic visits the bakery under the pretext of ordering prom desserts, really to escape his father's expectations. He watches Wren work and feels something loosen. He lingers too long; Wren pretends not to notice. Emotional beat: longing neither will name.

chapters.title: Rules of the Chat
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The five finally meet in person at the diner and compare notes: none of them added each other. They set rules—no telling adults, no using predictions for gain. Wren breaks rule two immediately, baking a 'warning' loaf for the crash victim's family. Emotional beat: complicity becoming community.

chapters.title: What the Bread Knows
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren's baked goods start echoing the chat's messages—a cinnamon swirl shaped like a lightning strike hours before one hits the school. Dad notices Wren's distraction; a tender, clumsy conversation about Wren's late mother hints she 'knew things' too. Emotional beat: inheritance of a gift and its burden.

chapters.title: Prom Court Politics
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic's father demands he run for prom king as a campaign stop for his mayoral race. Dominic nominates Wren for court instead, publicly, impulsively—an act of rebellion disguised as kindness. Wren panics in front of everyone. Emotional beat: visibility arriving unwanted.

chapters.title: The Third Message
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The chat goes silent for six days, then posts: 'The gym burns on prom night.' Panic fractures the group—Priya wants to cancel prom, Theo wants to tell someone, Dominic refuses to let his father's event become a target. Emotional beat: unity cracking under stakes.

chapters.title: Labels
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A classmate outs Wren's pronouns mockingly in the hallway; Dominic shuts it down hard, standing beside Wren in full view of the school. That night Wren bakes all night, furious and grateful, and finally texts Dominic something honest. Emotional beat: shame transmuting into defiance.

chapters.title: Investigation, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya traces the chat's origin to an account created the day Wren's mother died. Confronted, Wren admits the timeline—and the possibility that the chat connects to her. The group's trust wobbles; Theo defends Wren fiercely, an old wound reopening toward healing. Emotional beat: suspicion giving way to loyalty.

chapters.title: Dress Fitting
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Forced onto prom court, Wren endures a fitting where nothing off the rack fits right, until Dominic's aunt alters a suit instead of a dress without being asked. It's the first time an adult has simply gotten it. Wren cries in a fitting room and lets them. Emotional beat: being seen and surviving it.

chapters.title: Fire Drill
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic tests evacuation plans and discovers the gym's alarm system was quietly defunded by—his father's budget cuts. The prediction isn't fate; it's negligence waiting to happen. Dominic decides to run against his father's narrative, not for him. Emotional beat: duty inverted into conscience.

chapters.title: The Loaf Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren bakes a loaf that comes out wrong—burnt edges, hollow center—and understands it as a warning about themselves: stay hidden and burn out empty. They confess to the chat that they've been terrified of being known their whole life. Emotional beat: confession as turning point.

chapters.title: Theo's Amendment
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo formally apologizes to Wren for middle school, in person, badly, sincerely. Wren doesn't forgive him yet—but hands him a bread roll, which in Ravensworth language is a start. The found family solidifies around this small repair. Emotional beat: forgiveness beginning as an offering.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Three days out, the chat posts a final message: 'Only if he stays.' No name. The group races to figure out who 'he' is while preparing countermeasures—fire extinguishers, a changed venue petition, Priya's evidence file on the alarms. Emotional beat: dread braided with resolve.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic confronts his father about the alarms; the fight goes nuclear, and his father threatens to disown the 'distraction' Dominic has become. Dominic walks out and shows up at the bakery's back door, flour-dusted and wrecked. Wren lets him in. Emotional beat: choosing each other over approval.

chapters.title: Prom
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Prom begins—string lights, Wren's dessert table, Wren in the altered suit, hand in Dominic's. Then the smell of smoke. The 'he' from the prophecy is revealed: the janitor, Mr. Reyes, trapped near the old storage room where wiring frays. Emotional beat: joy interrupted by the predicted hour arriving.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. The group executes their plan: Priya triggers the alarm manually, Theo guides students out, Dominic pulls the breaker, and Wren—terrified, visible, loud—leads Mr. Reyes out through the loading door they scouted. The gym smolders but holds. Emotional beat: fear converted into action.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In the parking lot, ash on their suit, Wren is surrounded by classmates who now know their name. The chat sends one last message: 'Thread archived. You won't need us anymore.' Grief and relief tangle—losing the mystery, keeping the people. Emotional beat: bittersweet release.

chapters.title: Crumb by Crumb
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Weeks later, the five keep meeting anyway, chat renamed 'The Crumb (Just Friends Now).' Dominic's father faces the audit; Dominic moves into his aunt's spare room and smiles more. Theo and Wren rebuild slowly, one shared shift at the bakery at a time. Emotional beat: ordinary happiness earned.

chapters.title: The First Loaf of Summer
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. On the last day of school, Wren bakes a new recipe—open-crumbed, golden, sweet—and names it after the five of them. Dominic reads the card aloud. Wren, once invisible, stands in the doorway of their own life and welcomes people in. Emotional beat: belonging, fully claimed.
